DAAN.definition: Old, ancient: said of inanimate objects.

DADAEL.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dadaelen dayta relos ko.

DADAEL.definition: To be destroyed, ruined, damaged, spoiled.

DADANES.eng_example: He was the one who insulted us.
It is hard to be insulted.

DADANG.definition: To go near a fire or any other source of heat.
DADANG.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agdadang ta dikanto nga agpanateng.
DADANG.eng_example: Don’t go near a fire for you might catch cold.

DADANG.ilok_example: Mangidadang ka ti danum nga pagdigus ko.
DADANG.eng_example: Heat some water for my bath.

DADAPILAN.definition: Sugar mill; a machine with rollers used to press out the juice of the sugar cane, operated by a water buffalo attached to the end of the beam (TANGBAW) walking in a circle.

DADDADIAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: far from both speaker and hearer.

DADDAYDI.definition: That only, nothing but that: no longer extant, remote in time.

DADDUMA.ilok_example: Napan ti dadduma kadagiti sangaili mi idiay kusina.
DADDUMA.eng_example: Some of our guests went to the kitchen.

DAEG.definition: Nice, graceful, elegant, majestic, grand, stately.

DAEL.definition: Inasmuch as, it is well that, it is fortunate that.
DAEL.ilok_example: Dael na pay ketdi ta nabaknang da.
DAEL.eng_example: It is well that they are rich.

DAGA.definition: 1. Earth, soil, ground. 2. Land, especially agricultural land. 3. Country.
DAGA.eng_example: The child lay on the ground.

phrases.translation: What country did you come from?

DAGAANG.definition: Sweltering hot, sultry: said of the weather.
To be sweltering hot, sultry: said of the weather.
To feel sweltering hot, sultry: said of persons and animals.
DAGAANG.eng_example: That young woman feels sweltering hot.

DAGADAG.definition: To insist upon, press for, or urge.
DAGADAG.ilok_example: Isu ti nangidagadag iti panagbangon ti eskuela ditoy barrio mi.
DAGADAG.eng_example: He was the one who pressed for the construction of a schoolhouse in our barrio or village.

DAGAS.definition: To stop by, pass by, drop in for a while.
To stop by for, to pick up, to stop by and fetch.
DAGAS.eng_example: Stop by and fetch me when you go.

DAGAS.ilok_example: Idagas mo daytoy idiay balay da intono mapan ka idiay plasa.
DAGAS.eng_example: Will you deliver this to their house when you go to the plaza?

DAGDAG.definition: To hurry up someone, to impel or incite someone to act with greater speed.
To hurry up, to impel or incite to greater speed.
DAGDAG.eng_example: Incite Rose to greater speed in washing clothes.

DAGEM.definition: To take or do something intensely or seriously, to engage (oneself) on something intensely or seriously.
DAGEM.ilok_example: Saan mo nga idagem ta bagim ti trabaho.
DAGEM.eng_example: Don’t engage yourself in your work intensely.

DAGIDI.definition: Plural of DAYDI: in, at, to, of those (which are now extinct).

DAGINSEN.ilok_example: Daginsenem dagita lupot tapno makaanay dayta kahon.
DAGINSEN.eng_example: Press down the clothes so that the box will be adequate to contain them.

DAGINSEN.definition: To pack tightly or closely, to pile up neatly or tightly.
DAGINSEN.eng_example: Pile up those pieces of wood neatly here.

DAGITA.definition: Plural of DAYTA: in, at, to, of those (near hearer).

DAGSEN.definition: 1. Heavy, ponderous. 2. Weighty, important, serious, deep, profound. 3. Grievous, burdened. 4. Sluggish, slow or dull from loss of vitality.

phrases.phrase: Nadagsen ti nakem ko nga napan.
phrases.translation: My mind was burdened when I went.

DAGULLIT.definition: To do often, to do repeatedly.
DAGULLIT.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dagulliten dayta nga aramid mo.
DAGULLIT.eng_example: Don’t do that act of yours repeatedly.

DAGULLIT.definition: Importunate, overly persistent in request or demand.

DAGUMDAGUM.definition: Sting of bees, wasps, and other stinging insects.

DAGUP.ilok_example: Mano ti dagup ti botos na?
DAGUP.eng_example: What is the total of his votes?

DAGUP.definition: To sum or add up, to total.
DAGUP.ilok_example: Dagupem amin nga utang ko kenka.
DAGUP.eng_example: Total all my debts to you.

DAGUS.definition: Immediately, at once, directly, straightaway, forthwith.
To lodge, to stay or live in temporarily.
DAGUS.ilok_example: Agdagus ka idiay balay mi intono mapan ka idiay ili.
DAGUS.eng_example: Lodge in our house when you go to town.

DAIB.definition: To dive and get, dive for.
To dive with in order to put or give.

DAIG.definition: To have tuberculosis, to be sick with tuberculosis.
DAIG.ilok_example: Agdaig ti pusa no makasida iti siit ti igat.
DAIG.eng_example: A cat will have tuberculosis if it eats the bones of an eel.

DAIT.eng_example: He knows how to sew garments.

DAIT.ilok_example: Daytoy nga badok ti dinait na.
DAIT.eng_example: This is my dress which he sewed.

DAKES.definition: 1. Bad, evil, wicked, sinful. 2. Defective, faulty; unsound; damaged, spoiled.

phrases.phrase: Dakes ti nagatang ko nga kotse.
phrases.translation: The car that I bought is defective.

DAKIWAS.definition: To go to one after the other or to each one purposefully.
DAKIWAS.ilok_example: Isuda ti nagdakiwas kadagiti balbalay nga adda baboy na.
DAKIWAS.eng_example: They were the ones who went to each one of the houses which have pigs.

DAKKEL.definition: 1. To become big, large. 2. To grow up.
DAKKEL.ilok_example: Mangan ka ti adu tapno dardaras ka dumakkel.
DAKKEL.eng_example: Eat much so that you will grow up fast.

DAKLIS.definition: A kind of seine used for fishing in the sea near the shore.

DALAGA.definition: A pullet; a female animal at the age of puberty.

DALAGAN.definition: 1. The period after childbirth during which the mother is restricted from going out of her room. 2. The inclined bed in which the mother stays most of the time during this period.
To spend this period, to be in this period.

DALAGUDUG.definition: A kind of tree whose branches are used for fencing and whose flowers are sometimes eaten.

DALAN.eng_example: It was he who advised me.

DALAPUS.definition: To collide with a spirit or ghost, to become sick because of colliding with a spirit or ghost.

DALAYAP.definition: 1. A kind of citrus tree (Citrus lima Lunan). 2. The fruit of this tree.

DALAYDAY.definition: To hang in a careless or disorderly manner on a clothesline, a fence, etc.
To be hung in a careless or disorderly manner.

DALAYUDOY.definition: To be spongy, pulpy: said of meat, fish, fruits, etc.
DALAYUDOY.ilok_example: Agdalayudoy diay ikan nga nagatang ko.
DALAYUDOY.eng_example: The fish/meat that I bought was spongy.

DALDAL.definition: To soil, sully, besmirch especially by dragging on a dirty surface.

DALIASAT.eng_example: We cross an ocean when we go to their place.

DALIKEPKEP.definition: To cross the arms on the breast.
To hold with the arms around against the breast, to hug like a bear.
DALIKEPKEP.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dalikepkepan dayta ubing.
DALIKEPKEP.eng_example: Don’t hold the child with your arms around against your breast.

DALIMANEK.definition: To put things in order, to arrange things neatly.
DALIMANEK.eng_example: He knows how to put things in order.

DALIMANEK.ilok_example: Nadalimanek ti ayan ti panganan da.
DALIMANEK.eng_example: The place where they eat is orderly.

DALIMUGTONG.eng_example: Pile up those pieces of wood here.

DALINGDING.definition: To drape, provide with a curtain.

DALIPATU.definition: A flake of fire, especially one floating in the air; a flying ember.

DALLOT.definition: A kind of native song or chant.

DALLUYON.definition: A wave breaking into foam; a breaker.

DALUBDUB.definition: To prick, to pierce slightly with a sharp point.

DALUBDUB.eng_example: My foot was pricked by a thorn.

DALUBDUB.definition: The result of being pricked slightly; a prick.

DALUNGDONG.definition: To cover the head with this.
To cover someone’s head with this.

DALUPINGPING.definition: To gather up, draw together a section of one’s skirt.
DALUPINGPING.eng_example: Gather up a section of your skirt.

DALUPINGPING.definition: To gather up or draw together a section of one’s skirt and tuck this in the waist.
DALUPINGPING.eng_example: Gather up a section of your skirt and tuck this in your waist.

DALUPISAK.definition: To sit on one’s haunches on the floor.

DALUSON.definition: To gather, bring or put together.

DALUTAYTAY.definition: To be weak, feeble, exhausted; hence, to swoon or collapse due to weakness or exhaustion.

DAMA.definition: To play draughts or checkers with.

At the present time, presently, right now, at this very moment, currently.

DAMA.definition: In a little while, by and by, soon.
DAMA.eng_example: I will wash those in a little while.

DAMAG.definition: To ask for news, information, rumor, or gossip.

DAMAG.eng_example: Inquire when he is coming back.

DAMIT.definition: To receive or collect the benefits or rewards of, to profit from, to reap or enjoy the benefits of.

DANAG.definition: To worry, be worried, anxious, troubled, uneasy.

DANGGAY.definition: To accompany, especially with a musical instrument.

DANIW.definition: To sing, especially ditties or native chants.

phrases.translation: Don't report that news to him.

examples.definition: A dish consisting of roasted fish boiled in water and seasoned with sour fruits or vegetables.
Itchiness between the toes or fingers caused by prolonged soaking in water.

DAO.definition: A kind of tree (Dracontomelon dao) which gives valuable timber.

DAP-AW.definition: To step in for a moment, to pay a short visit.

DAPADAP.definition: To feel or explore by touching with the hand.
DAPADAP.eng_example: Feel that floor with your hand.

DAPAG.definition: To place, put, or set down squarely, firmly, or solidly.

DAPAK.definition: To make a flapping or trotting sound especially when walking.

DAPANDAPAN.definition: A kind of native cake shaped like the sole of a foot.

DAPIG.definition: To hit with the flat side of a large knife (BUNENG).

DAPIL.definition: To press out the juice of sugarcane using a machine with rollers called DADAPILAN.
To press out the juice of sugarcane in the DADAPILAN.
DAPIL.eng_example: He pressed out the juice of my sugarcane in the DADAPILAN.

DAPIL.definition: Half-rounded, semicircular, flattish: said especially of the shape of the head.

DAPILAG.definition: A kind of shallow basket, more or less resembling a big winnowing basket.

DAPILUS.eng_example: He caused the table to collapse.

DAPLA.definition: To lie prone especially with the arms spread.

DAR-AW.definition: To look at or watch from an elevated position, to look down at.

DARADDAN.definition: To do one after the other, to do successively.

DARAGUP.definition: To join together, unite; to pile up, accumulate.

DARANGIDANGAN.definition: Ripening, almost ripe, nearly ripe: said of fruits.

DARANUDOR.definition: To make a roaring or rumbling sound.
DARANUDOR.eng_example: The truck made a roaring sound.

DARAS.eng_example: How many times did he come back?

DARAS.definition: 1. Easy, not difficult; fast. 2. Often, frequently.
DARAS.eng_example: It is easy to read your book.

DARAS.definition: Quickly, rapidly, swiftly, fast; immediately, promptly.

DARASUDOS.definition: To do hastily, hurriedly, rashly; to rush.

DARISAY.definition: Of good quality, pure, clear: said of the climate, air, etc.

DARISON.definition: To push oneself in, to squeeze in.
To push, cram, or squeeze in.
DARISON.ilok_example: Isu ti nangidarison kadagiti lupot ditoy.
DARISON.eng_example: He was the one who pushed in the clothes here.

DARONDON.definition: Producing a second crop: said of fruit-bearing trees.

DAROY.definition: Thin, watery, weak: said of gruel, chocolate, soup, and the like.

DARUMISA.definition: Clumsy and dirty or slovenly: as, to spill food, drink, water, when washing the dishes.

DARUNDUN.definition: To push (someone standing in a crowd or in line).

DARUP.definition: To come or approach impetuously or precipitately.
To go to or approach impetuously or precipitately.

DAS.ilok_example: Adda met la ngata umdas nga kired ti pakinakem na ket maitured nak nga palubosan?

DASAR.ilok_example: Dasaram ta lamisaan ta mangan tayon.
DASAR.eng_example: Set the table and let’s eat.

DASAR.definition: To set out or prepare for use.

DASAY.definition: To be weakened, overpowered, or prostrated (by sickness, drunkenness, etc.); to be caused to stay in bed or lie down.
DASAY.eng_example: He was caused to stay in bed by sickness.

DASI.definition: To slip and fall on the back, to fall supine.
DASI.eng_example: Be careful lest you might slip and fall on your back.

DASIG.definition: To separate into groups, classify and separate accordingly.

DATA.definition: To lie on one’s back, lie supine.
To cause someone to lie on their back.

DATAG.ilok_example: Indatag na ti papeles na kadagiti agtuturay.
DATAG.eng_example: He submitted his papers to the government officials.

DATAO.definition: 1. One (an indefinite pronoun). 2. I (an indirect pronoun for the first person singular).
DATAO.eng_example: One must rest a little / I must rest a little.

DATAR.definition: To display, exhibit, expose, show, present to view.

DATDATA.definition: That only, nothing but that: near the hearer.

DATDATAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: extant but not seen.

DATON.definition: To give, present, offer as a sacrifice or token of something.

DAULO.definition: To lead, direct, guide, be in the vanguard of.

DAULO.eng_example: It was he who led our group.

To make a detour to or a brief stop in (a place) in order to get (something or someone), to go to (a place) for a moment in order to get (something or someone).

DAW-AS.definition: To make a detour to or a brief stop at (a place) in order to give or deliver (something or someone), to go to (a place) for a moment in order to deliver or give (something or someone).
DAW-AS.ilok_example: Idaw-as mo man diay ragadi mi idiay balay da.
DAW-AS.eng_example: Will you please make a detour to their house and deliver our saw.

DAWA.definition: An ear of grain, especially of rice; spike.
To develop spikes: said especially of rice.

DAWADAW.definition: To jut, project, protrude, stick out; to exceed in length or height.

DAWADAW.eng_example: There is a piece of wood jutting from the top of their house.

DAWADAW.definition: To project; to cause to stick out, jut, protrude; to cause to be longer (as the wick of a lamp).
DAWADAW.eng_example: Cause that piece of wood to stick out.

DAWAT.ilok_example: Kayat na ti dumawat ti bawang.
DAWAT.eng_example: He wants to ask for garlic.

DAWI.eng_example: I have been here for a long time but not one has taken a bite at my bait.

DAWI.ilok_example: Daytoy ti nadawi nga aramiden na.
DAWI.eng_example: This is what he usually does.

DAYA.definition: To have a feast, festival, or banquet.
Exposed, laid bare, presented to view.

DAYAS.definition: To use to wash, bathe, or cleanse; to wash, bathe, or cleanse with.
DAYAS.ilok_example: Danum nga napudot ti idayas mo ti dayta sugat na.
DAYAS.eng_example: Wash his wound with hot water.

DAYAW.definition: To honor, respect; to show respect or reverence for; to esteem, revere; to praise, exalt.
1. Respectful, polite, courteous. 2. Great, grand, eminent, illustrious.

DAYDAY.ilok_example: Idayday mo dagita lupot tapno agmaga da.
DAYDAY.eng_example: Spread the clothes so that they will get dry.

DAYDI.definition: That, that one: no longer extant, remote in time.

DAYDIAY.definition: 1. That, that one: far from both speaker and hearer. 2. Of that, of that one: far from both speaker and hearer.

DAYENGDENG.definition: To complain about, scold, rebuke, reprimand.

DAYO.definition: To compete with each other, to rival each other.

DAYO.definition: To compete or vie with (in a contest, athletic meet, etc.).

DAYTA.definition: 1. That, that one: near the hearer. 2. Of that, of that one: near the hearer.

DAYTAY.definition: 1. That, that one: extant but not seen. 2. Of that, of that one: extant but not seen.

To sing (a song) by humming and mumbling the lyrics.

examples.eng_example: The people were equipped with arms and were wearing uniforms.

DEDDEDIAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: far from both speaker and hearer.

DEDDEYDI.definition: That only, nothing but that: no longer extant, remote in time.

DEDDEYDIAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: far from both speaker and hearer.

DEDEDIAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: far from both speaker and hearer.

DEDETAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: extant but not seen.

DEDI.definition: That: no longer extant, remote in time.

DEDIAY.definition: That: far from both speaker and hearer.

DEGDEG.definition: To increase in degree or intensity; to worsen.
To cause to increase in degree or intensity; to make worse.

DEL-AG.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agdelag ta dinto ket makariing diay ubing.
DEL-AG.eng_example: Don’t shout lest the child wake up.

DELIKADO.definition: 1. Delicate, frail, weak. 2. Serious, grave. 3. Having or showing a sensitive distaste for anything offensive or improper. 4. Dangerous, perilous, uncertain.

phrases.phrase: Delikado la unay dayta anak mo.

DEMDEM.ilok_example: Nabayag nga demdemdemen na ti pungtot na.
DEMDEM.eng_example: He has been repressing his anger for a long time now.

DENDEN.definition: To move by sliding, as when one is sitting on a bench; to go or come nearer a certain point.
DENDEN.ilok_example: Dumenden ka man bassit ta makatugawak met.
DENDEN.eng_example: Will you please move a little bit so that I can sit down also.

DENDEN.definition: To move (someone or something) by sliding toward a certain point.

DENGDENG.definition: To cook (vegetables) into a vegetable dish.

DENGNGEG.definition: 1. To listen to, pay attention to; hence, 2. To heed, obey.
DENGNGEG.eng_example: Listen to what they are saying.

DENGNGEG.ilok_example: Indiak nga mangngeg ti boses mo.

DENGNGEP.definition: To apply ointment, poultice, and the like (to an injury).

DENNET.definition: To put in contact with, to cause to come in contact with.
DENNET.ilok_example: Saan mo nga idennet dayta badom dita kape.
DENNET.eng_example: Don’t cause your dress to come in contact with the coffee.

DENNET.ilok_example: Aluadam no maidennet ta imam dita agburburek nga danum.
DENNET.eng_example: Be careful lest your hand come in contact with the boiling water.

DEPDEP.definition: To extinguish, put out (a fire or light).

DEPPA.definition: Span or distance measured by both arms extended sideways.
To measure by both arms extended sideways.

DEPPAAG.ilok_example: Tallo nga balay ti dimpaag kalpasan ti uram.
DEPPAAG.eng_example: Three houses collapsed after the fire.

DEPPAAG.definition: To cause to collapse or topple.
DEPPAAG.ilok_example: Saan nga deppaagen ti angin dayta abulog yo ta nalagda.
DEPPAAG.eng_example: The wind won’t cause your fence to collapse for it is strong.

DEPPEL.definition: To imprint or put one’s thumbprint.
To press on, apply pressure on.

DEPPES.definition: To cause to bend backward; to push down or close to the surface.

DERDER.definition: To cause to become pulpy by beating, cooking, etc.
To become pulpy due to beating, overcooking, etc.

DESDES.definition: To be streaked with, have trails of.

DETA.definition: That, that one: near the hearer.

DETAY.definition: That, that one: extant but not seen.

DETDETA.definition: That only, nothing but that: near the hearer.

DETDETAY.definition: That only, nothing but that: extant but not seen.

DEYDI.definition: That, that one: no longer extant, remote in time.

DEYDIAY.definition: That, that one: far from both speaker and hearer.

DEYTA.definition: That, that one: near the hearer.

DEYTAY.definition: That, that one: extant but not seen.

DI.definition: A particle expressing indifference, defiance, or encouragement.
DI.ilok_example: Di makitaray ka no isu ti kayat mo.
DI.eng_example: Then elope (with someone) if that is what you want to do.

DIABLES.definition: Form of diablo used in cursing.
DIABLES.ilok_example: Naggaset ket ti diables nga Paulon.
DIABLES.eng_example: That devil Paul is indeed very lucky.

DIAKET.definition: To use or wear a jacket.

DIARYO.definition: To appear or be published in a newspaper.

DIASKE.definition: A curse word synonymous with diables; devil.
DIASKE.ilok_example: Kasla napukaw nga asok ti diaske.

DIAY.definition: That; there; in, at, to that.

DIAYA.definition: To offer, give, or present as an act of worship or devotion.
DIAYA.ilok_example: Indiaya na amin nga kukua na nga pangtulong kadakuada.
DIAYA.eng_example: He offered all his properties in order to help them.

DIDAL.definition: To use or wear a thimble.

DIDIGRA.ilok_example: Nadidigra kami itay napalabas nga gerra.
DIDIGRA.eng_example: We were scared during the past war.

DIDING.definition: To provide with a wall, put a wall to.
DIDING.ilok_example: Didingan mi daytoy balay mi inton bigat.
DIDING.eng_example: We will put a wall to our house tomorrow.

DIGO.definition: 1. Broth; the liquid of a dish. 2. Coconut water.

DIGOS.definition: To take a bath, to bathe oneself.
DIGOS.eng_example: They are going to take a bath in the river.

DIGOS.definition: To give (a person or animal) a bath, to bathe (a person or animal).
DIGOS.ilok_example: Mapan da digosen diay nuang da idiay waig.
DIGOS.eng_example: They are going to bathe their water buffalo in the brook.

DIKEN.definition: Pad: a circlet of cloth placed on top of the head on which a load is set; this protects the crown of the head from injury and at the same time stabilizes the load.

DIKET.definition: 1. Sticky or glutinous rice. 2. Sticky variety of corn. 3. Sticky variety of cassava.

DIKIDIK.ilok_example: Dikidiken na dayta nakirog nga bagas.
DIKIDIK.eng_example: He will grind that toasted rice into powder.

DIKKI.definition: Soft deposit on the surface of the teeth, as when one does not brush his teeth.

DIKORASION.definition: To decorate or adorn with, to use as decoration.

DILAMUT.definition: To gather with difficulty from a scant supply; to scrape; to benefit or be given a share of something that is scant or meager.
DILAMUT.ilok_example: Awan ti nadilamutan mi ti daydiay inted na nga kuarta.
DILAMUT.eng_example: We were not given a share of the money that he gave.

DILAP.definition: To flood, inundate; to have a flood.
To stick out one's tongue at someone.
To stick out one's tongue at (someone).
DILAP.eng_example: It was he at whom he stuck out his tongue.

DILAT.definition: To stick out one's tongue at someone.

DILDIL.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dildilan dayta pinggan.

DILI.ilok_example: Ammo na ti nadili nga paset ti dalan.
DILI.eng_example: He knows the stony stretch of the road.

DILLAW.definition: 1. To notice, observe, see, perceive. 2. To call attention to, remark or comment on; to criticize, complain about.
DILLAW.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dildillawen ti pannangan na.
DILLAW.eng_example: Don’t notice or make any comment on his manner of eating.

DILLAW.definition: To notice or observe by chance; to perceive.
DILLAW.ilok_example: Nadlaw ko nga adda kayat na nga ibaga diay baro.
DILLAW.eng_example: I noticed by chance that the young man wants to say something.

DINANUMAN.definition: A dish consisting of roasted fish boiled in water and seasoned with sour fruits or vegetables.

DINGO.definition: To take care of, to feed; to raise (animals).
DINGO.eng_example: It was he who fed the pig.

DINGOEN.definition: Animals, especially hogs, raised for meat; domestic animals.

DINGPIL.ilok_example: Dingpilen yo dagita pias tapno maikkat ti tubbog na.
DINGPIL.eng_example: Squeeze those sour fruits so as to remove their juice.

DINNA.definition: To put or place oneself at the side of, to go and stay at the side of.
DINNA.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dinnaan dayta balasang ko.
DINNA.eng_example: Don’t go and stay at the side of my daughter.

DINOMINGGO.definition: Every week, weekly, by the week.

DINUYDUY.definition: A kind of sweet made of boiled ripe squash mixed with coconut meat and either sugar or salt.

DIPAS.eng_example: The bananas were consumed in a short time.

DIPPIG.definition: A kind of banana which is flat in shape, usually boiled or fried before it is eaten.

DIPPIT.ilok_example: Saan ka nga dumippit kadagita agtartarabaho.
DIPPIT.eng_example: Don’t press near those who are working.

DIPPIT.ilok_example: Uray la nga agdidipiit ti tao ti kaadu ti nagbuya.
DIPPIT.eng_example: The people were pressed together due to the great number of those who went to see the show.

DIPPIT.ilok_example: Saan mo nga dippiten dayta badok.

DIRAM-US.eng_example: As soon as you wake up wash your face.

DIRAM-US.ilok_example: Diram-usam dayta kabsat mo intono makariing.
DIRAM-US.eng_example: Wash the face of your brother (or sister) when he (or she) wakes up.

DISGRASIA.definition: 1. To inflict injury on, to cause to have an accident or misfortune. 2. To assault or molest sexually.
1. To meet with a misfortune or accident, to be injured. 2. To be assaulted or molested sexually.

DISKURSO.definition: To make a speech or oration.

DISMAYA.definition: To be upset, perturbed, discomposed, distressed.

DISNUG.definition: To hit with the fists; to punch.

DISSAAG.definition: To get down or off, alight, descend, dismount.
To take, put, or place down from a higher place.

DISSAAR.definition: To put or place on the floor.
DISSAAR.eng_example: Place that child on the floor.

DISSO.ilok_example: Immuna nga impabuya da dagiti napintas nga disso ditoy Pilipinas.
DISSO.eng_example: They first showed the beautiful spots in the Philippines.

DISSO.definition: To alight, to set (on a place), to land.
DISSO.eng_example: The bird alighted on my shoulder.

DISSOOR.definition: To cause to fall suddenly and heavily, to put down suddenly and heavily.
DISSOOR.ilok_example: Isu ti nangidissoor ti dakkel nga kahon.
DISSOOR.eng_example: It was he who put down the big box suddenly and heavily.

DISTURBO.ilok_example: Saan nak man nga disturboen ta adu ti trabahok.
DISTURBO.eng_example: Please don’t disturb me for I have much work to do.

DIWIG.definition: 1. Wry, twisted, contorted: said of the mouth of a person, a jar, a basket, etc. 2. Crooked, not straight: said of the way an object is cut. 3. Having a wry mouth: said of a person.

DODOL.definition: A kind of pudding made of rice (either ground or pounded into powder), coconut milk (getta), and sugar.

DODOOMEN.definition: Rice near maturity whose grain is already fully formed.

DON.definition: 1. Sir; Mr.: a title of respect, used with the first name. 2. A distinguished man.

DONYA.definition: 1. Madam; Mrs.: a title of respect, used with the first name. 2. A distinguished woman. 3. Rat, mouse (euphemistic).

DOOL.definition: To feed, especially by putting the food to the mouth.

DOOM.definition: To eat or chew immature rice or uncooked rice after removing the husk.
To eat or chew (immature rice or uncooked rice after removing the husk).

DOOY.definition: Wanting attention, care, or show of affection: usually said of children.
DOOY.eng_example: You are a child who wants so much attention.

DRAM.definition: Drum: a barrellike metal container for oil, etc.

DUBLI.definition: To repeat, to do, say, etc. again.

DUDA.definition: To have doubts, be doubtful, suspicious.

DUGDUG.definition: To decay, decompose, rot, dissolve, melt.

DUGMAM.definition: To cause to fall forward or prone.

DUGMON.definition: Nest of a wild boar or a hog.
To wallow, to roll oneself about in an indolent or ungainly manner.
To collect or gather leaves, twigs, etc. for making a nest or bed.

DUGUL.definition: A hump, protuberance, swelling; a node.

DUKANG.definition: Bulky, piled in a big heap.

DUKINAR.ilok_example: Apay nga dukinaren yo dagita lupot?
DUKINAR.eng_example: Why are you strewing around the clothes?

DUKIT.definition: To reopen a subject, to mention again; to recall, to remind someone of.
DUKIT.ilok_example: Saan mo nga idukit dayta ta nalipatakon.
DUKIT.eng_example: Don’t mention that again for I have already forgotten it.

DUKLUS.eng_example: It was he who attacked me.

DUKO.definition: To recur: said of an ailment, hunger, etc.
DUKO.ilok_example: Madanaganak no dumuko ti sakit ko.
DUKO.eng_example: I am worried lest my sickness recurs.

DUKOL.definition: To produce a hump disclosing its presence; to protrude, jut out.
DUKOL.eng_example: What is that producing a hump on the mat?

DUKOT.definition: To be worried, distressed, uneasy, perturbed, anxious, impatient.

DUKYANG.definition: A kind of small clam found in brooks and rivers.

DULIAN.eng_example: He has not a distinguishing trait.

DULIDUL.definition: To urge, press, insist, or force on (someone).
DULIDUL.ilok_example: Saan mo nga idulidul kanyak dayta saan ko nga kayat.
DULIDUL.eng_example: Don’t force on me that which I don’t like.

DULIN.definition: To hide, stay away from view.
DULIN.eng_example: You hide and I will look for you.

DULIN.definition: To hide or keep away from view (someone or something).
To put away, put aside (plates or bedding).

DUMA.definition: To differ, be different, dissimilar, unlike.

DUMADUMA.ilok_example: Nadumaduma nga nateng ti immula da.

DUMDUMA.definition: To be regarded differently, to be distinguishable, to stand out.

DUMUG.definition: To bend or incline the head, to bow; to look down.
DUMUG.eng_example: He looked down when he saw me.

DUMUG.definition: To bend or incline down, to cause to bend or incline down.

DUNG-AW.definition: To wail, lament, mourn aloud which may include singing a dirge.

DUNGDUNG.definition: A very large pot used for cooking rice, meat, vegetables, etc.

DUNGER.definition: To shake the head forward and backward rapidly, to nod rapidly and continuously.
To have the head drop forward involuntarily due to drowsiness, etc.

DUNGET.definition: To cut near or close to the trunk, origin, or beginning.
DUNGET.ilok_example: Isu ti nangidunget ti sanga ti kayo.
DUNGET.eng_example: It was he who cut close the branches of the tree.

DUNGIR.definition: To get hurt, injured, or bruised.
DUNGIR.ilok_example: Saan ka nga agtartaray ta dikanto madungiran.
DUNGIR.eng_example: Don’t run for you might get hurt.

DUNGNGO.eng_example: I shall love you very, very deeply.

DUNGRIT.definition: Filthy, dirty, untidy, especially on the face.

DUNGSO.definition: To crash (oneself or itself) into, to ram (oneself or itself) against, to cause (oneself) to collide with.
DUNGSO.eng_example: Why did you collide with me?

DUNGSO.definition: To crash into, ram against, collide with.
DUNGSO.ilok_example: Naidungso diay lugan da ti poste.
DUNGSO.eng_example: Their vehicle crashed into a post.

DUNGSOL.definition: To hit with a blacksmith's hammer.
To use as a blacksmith's hammer, to hit (someone or something) with this.

DUPAG.definition: To repeat, do again, say again.
DUPAG.eng_example: Will you please repeat what you said to me.

DUPIR.definition: To push, shove, or move to (a place).
DUPIR.ilok_example: Idupir mo dayta bangko dita diding.
DUPIR.eng_example: Push that bench to that wall.

DUPUDUP.definition: To be, go, or come together.
DUPUDUP.ilok_example: Nagdudupudup da nga immay gimmatang ti lupot.
DUPUDUP.eng_example: They came together to buy clothes.

DUREK.definition: To have pus in the ear.

DURI.definition: Spinal column, vertebral column, spine, backbone.

DURUDOR.definition: 1. To put on a spit. 2. To poke with a spit.

DUSAG.definition: To elbow, hit with the elbow.
DUSAG.eng_example: Don’t hit me with your elbow.

DUTDUT.definition: Full of feathers or body hair.
To remove the feathers of, to dress (a chicken, etc.).
To extract, draw out, pick off.

DUTOK.ilok_example: Ni Pedro ti dinutokan mi nga presidente.

DUTOK.definition: To be appointed, designated, assigned (as president, etc.).

DUYOG.definition: 1. Half of a coconut shell used as a dish. 2. A dish.

DUYOK.definition: To produce or cause a sharp or stabbing pain.
DUYOK.ilok_example: Dumuyok manen ti sakit na daytoy tian ko.
DUYOK.eng_example: My stomach ailment is producing again a sharp pain.

DUYOK.ilok_example: Dinuyok na daydiay baboy ti natirad nga imuko.
DUYOK.eng_example: He stabbed the pig with a sharp knife.

DUYOS.definition: That to which one’s feelings, sympathy, etc. flows.
DUYOS.eng_example: It is he to whom my feelings flow.

DISNOG.definition: to hit with the fists; to punch.
